Root cause of agent-team.ts preference persistence bug: `sanitizeJson()` (line 110) replaces ALL newline characters in the raw JSON file with literal `
` escape sequences, including structural whitespace newlines between JSON tokens. Since `savePreferences()` (line 546) writes pretty-printed JSON with `JSON.stringify(merged, null, 2) + "
"`, the saved file has real newlines. On the next `loadPreferences()` call, `sanitizeJson()` converts those structural newlines to literal `
`, producing `{
  "viewMode": "compact"
}
` which is invalid JSON. The `catch {}` on line 531 silently swallows the parse error and returns `{}`, so viewMode falls back to the default "cards". The bug is that sanitizeJson is designed for sanitizing JSON string values but is being applied to the entire JSON document.

Reviewed routine issue duplication fix (2026-04-07): Third fallback in findLiveExecutionIssue catches open issues with no live heartbeat run. Key insight: the unique constraint `issues_open_routine_execution_uq` only applies when `executionRunId IS NOT NULL`, so issues created by routine dispatch (which don't set executionRunId) are NOT protected by the constraint — meaning the third fallback is the only thing preventing duplicates in that scenario. The test correctly verifies the "open issue + completed run → coalesce" path. The old test name and expectations were simply inverted to match new behavior. Also bundled in the diff: reconcileStaleRuns function (previously reviewed on 2026-04-05).

OpenClaw cron `delivery.mode: "announce"` ALWAYS delivers the agent's reply to Telegram — even "all clear" / "exit silently" messages. The watchdog skill was designed to be silent-when-healthy but has been sending ~8 deliveries including no-op messages because announce mode has no content filter. For the new audit job this is actually desired (always-send), but any future "alert-only" cron job should NOT use announce — use `mode: "none"` and have the agent call message tool directly when needed.

Key learning: the "NEVER wait for replies" line in the audit rules section is the critical architectural guardrail that prevents the impossible interactive-cron pattern.
